raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
This PR adds --update-weight-broadcast-mode to control how full weights are broadcast to rollout engines:

  • per-param (default): broadcasts each parameter separately.
  • flattened-bucket: packs each update bucket into a single byte tensor and broadcasts it once, reducing collective calls.

The flattened mode preserves mixed tensor dtypes and passes load_format="flattened_bucket" to SGLang for reconstruction and loading. The configuration is also forwarded through the tensor updater’s distributed path.

Flattened broadcasting requires --update-weight-mode=full, --update-weight-transport=nccl, and an SGLang implementation with multi-dtype FlattenedTensorBucket support.

Experimental results

We benchmarked weight updates for Qwen3-30B-A3B on Moore Threads S5000 GPUs in a disaggregated training and inference setup, with one node dedicated to training and one node dedicated to inference.

Broadcast mode | Average weight update time -- | -- per-param | 22.108 s flattened-bucket | 25.642 s

In this configuration, flattened broadcasting increased average weight update time by 3.534 s (15.99%).

Larger deployments and models may benefit more from fewer collective calls if communication overhead becomes dominant. However, this remains a hypothesis: additional benchmarks are needed to determine whether those savings outweigh packing and memory-copy costs as deployment size increases.

Validation

  • Added unit tests for argument parsing and rejection of incompatible update modes.
  • Python syntax and diff whitespace checks passed.
  • Measured weight update performance in the two-node S5000 configuration described above.

-            load_format=load_format,
